title: Retroactive credit approval exception queue and automation playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Enterprise deals sometimes require retroactive credits (manual adjustments) tied to negotiated SLA/contract clauses or security questionnaire hold-outs. Today these credits are handled ad hoc by Finance and Sales, creating long queues, inconsistent GL tagging, missed audits, and delayed invoices. Goal: design an exception queue + automated remediation path that preserves auditability, enforces approvals for > threshold credits, and automatically issues low-risk credits without manual intervention. Scope: covers credits initiated by Sales/CS/Finance for invoices within 90 days, interactions with security questionnaire holds, and credits tied to reserved capacity/proration for Dedicated customers. Out of scope: refunds that require legal settlement or court-ordered reversals.
acceptance_criteria: A queue exists in the billing app that captures all retro credit requests with metadata (contract id, invoice id, contract clause, requested amount, approver, requester)
Credits < $5,000 with matching audit tags and finance reconciliation pass are auto-approved and applied within 24 hours
Credits >= $5,000 route to a two-step approval (Finance + Sales Ops) with automatic ledger recording and notification
Security-questionnaire-related credits require Legal sign-off flag and are blocked until the security_review_required flag is cleared
All credits create an auditable event with links to source docs (contract PDF, SQ ticket, PRD) and a durable reason code for downstream analytics
A migration job clears the existing backlog (older than 30 days) and moves items to the new queue with preserved history
Monitoring: backlog size, time-to-apply median/95th, error rate, and reconciliation failure rate are visible on the billing dashboard
design_notes: Proposed flow: 1) Intake API: standardized POST payload from Sales/Finance UI or webhook capturing contract_id, invoice_id, requested_amount, reason_code, supporting_links. 2) Risk scoring service evaluates auto-approve eligibility (contract tier, prior disputes, customer_age, recent refunds). 3) Low-risk path triggers automated credit job that writes to billing ledger and emits invoice adjustment events. 4) High-risk items create an approval task in the exception queue UI for approvers. 5) Legal flagging: security questionnaire items set security_review_required=true and add 'Legal' to approvers; automated escalations if >48h. 6) Accounting integration writes entries to GL via our existing payments connector and tags entries for audit retention. Implementation constraints: existing invoice backend can only accept adjustment batches once per day; automated job must batch accordingly and provide dry-run preview. Ensure idempotency using request_id and immutable event IDs.
data_requirements: Data fields required: invoice_id, invoice_date, customer_org_id, contract_id, contract_version, requested_amount_usd, currency, requester_id, supporting_documents (URLs), security_questionnaire_ticket_id (optional), sales_order_id, ledger_account, request_id. We need a nightly sync from Billing warehouse to support reconciliation. Success metrics tracked in Looker: billing.credit_apply_rate, billing.backlog_count, billing.credit_reconciliation_failures.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilot): enable auto-approve for credits < $500 for a small set of internal enterprise customers and Finance team. Phase 2 (soft launch): expand to credits < $5,000 and invite Sales Ops to approve queue, collect metrics for 2 billing cycles. Phase 3 (full launch): enable for all eligible customers, enable migration job for backlog, retire ad hoc spreadsheet process. Communication: runbook for Finance, training session with Sales Ops, release notes in Console release-2026.04.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: auto-applied credits incorrectly assigned to wrong GL account. Mitigation: require ledger_account mapping at intake and verify with a validation job before apply. Risk: Legal delays on security-questionnaire credits blocking customer invoicing; Mitigation: add SLA escalation (48h) and fallback temporary invoice hold with audit trail. Risk: double-credit due to retry; Mitigation: enforce idempotency with request_id and a write-once event store.
